sections.h2: What is Forrest County, Mississippi, and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Forrest County is a Pine Belt county in southeast Mississippi whose county seat and largest city is Hattiesburg. It was created from Perry County in 1908 and is part of the Hattiesburg metropolitan area. Total area is 470 square miles, nearly all of it land.

Hattiesburg and Petal are the two cities, and a small part of Hattiesburg lies across the line in Lamar County. Smaller places include Glendale, Rawls Springs, Brooklyn, Carnes and McLaurin. Part of De Soto National Forest falls inside the county,. Rural parcels there are valued by the state differently from city lots, since agricultural land is valued by soil type and productivity.

sections.h2: Which roads and neighbors shape a Forrest County sale?
sections.html:
Interstate 59 and U.S. 11, 49 and 98 run through the county, along with Mississippi 13 and 42. Forrest County borders Jones, Perry, Stone, Pearl River, Lamar and Covington counties.

Because Hattiesburg straddles Forrest and Lamar counties, a buyer shopping on the west side of town can end up comparing two tax collectors, two assessors and different millage rates for houses a mile apart. The county line, plus the city of Hattiesburg or Petal levy, decides the bill. Ask the Forrest County Tax Collector which taxing districts apply to your parcel before you quote any monthly cost to a buyer.

Three public school systems operate here, so a Petal address and a Hattiesburg address attend different districts even when the homes look alike. Forrest County Agricultural High School is also in the county.

sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Forrest County?
sections.html:
The county has a Tax Assessor and a Tax Collector, and both offices are at 601 N. Main Street in downtown Hattiesburg. According to the county tax office page, the assessor must locate, classify and assess all taxable property each year, covering roughly 50,000 parcels of real and personal property.

  • Assessor phone: (601) 545-6130, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1626, Hattiesburg, MS 39403.
  • Collector phone: (601) 582-8228, with statements also handled through P.O. Box 1689, Hattiesburg, MS 39403.
  • The county maps its parcels on TSC Maps, which shows ownership, values, aerial views and legal descriptions.
  • The state requires new aerial photography every ten years, and Forrest County had new photos flown in early 2022.

The Mississippi Department of Revenue adds that assessors must revalue real property at least once every four years. The county tax rolls go to the Board of Supervisors, and the public can review them and file protests before the board and the state approve them.

sections.h2: How is a Forrest County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
The bill is true value, times the assessment ratio for the property class, times the millage rate set by the taxing bodies. Forrest County's collector applies the ratio and the levy set by the Board of Supervisors and the governing boards of Hattiesburg and Petal.

ClassPropertyRatio of true value
IOwner-occupied single-family home10%
IIOther real property15%
IIIPersonal property15%
IVPublic utilities30%
VMotor vehicles30%

As an example from the state's own FAQ, a Class II property with a true value of $10,000 is assessed at $1,500, and at 100 mills that produces $150 in tax. Your own millage depends on whether the house is in Hattiesburg, Petal or the unincorporated county, which we have not confirmed from an official rate sheet. The Department of Revenue publishes combined county and city millage schedules on its property tax data page.

sections.h2: When are Forrest County taxes due, and what about a deed you just recorded?
sections.html:
Mississippi taxes are due on or before February 1 for the property assessed the previous year, and if that date falls on a weekend or holiday you have until the following Monday. The county site also points out a quirk that affects sellers: the mapping staff work deeds from the previous year, and it can take up to a year for a new owner's name to appear on the land roll.

That lag means a buyer may receive a bill in the seller's name, and a seller may keep receiving statements after closing. Whoever signs the settlement statement should give the Tax Collector a new mailing address, since the office asks taxpayers to report all changes of address or mortgage status. Statements go to mortgage companies or to individuals on the mailing list.

Mobile and manufactured homes follow their own timeline. A mobile home must be registered within seven days of purchase, and the county says taxes are due within 90 days, then each year after. An owner can declare a mobile home as real property for a fee, which changes how it is assessed.

sections.h2: How does homestead exemption work in Forrest County?
sections.html:
Forrest County accepts homestead applications from January 2 to April 1, and the exemption is a one-time filing unless your situation changes. It does not apply to rental property.

TypeWho qualifiesBenefit
RegularUnder 65 and not disabledCredit of up to $300 against property taxes
SpecialAge 65 or older, or 100% disabledFirst $7,500 of assessed value exempt
Disabled veteran100% service-connected, and an unremarried spouseTotal exemption from ad valorem taxes

First-time filers bring the recorded deed, the purchase price and down payment, Social Security numbers for owners, and tag numbers for every vehicle, since vehicles must be registered in Forrest County before the application is accepted. A buyer who purchases your home needs to file in their own name, so tell them about the April 1 cutoff.

sections.h2: How do I contest an assessment in Forrest County?
sections.html:
You can talk with the assessor first, then protest to the Board of Supervisors. The assessor's page invites owners with a real concern to bring supporting documents, such as repair bids or photographs. The state advises requesting a hearing with the Board of Supervisors, with the Chancery Clerk as the contact, and says an appeal normally must be filed by the first Monday in August before the due date.

The county page says protests are accepted after the rolls are compiled and before the board approves them, without naming a date. We could not confirm a Forrest-specific August date, so treat the state's first Monday in August as the safe deadline and ask the office to confirm.

sections.h2: What happens if Forrest County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate taxes put the parcel at risk of a county tax sale. The Department of Revenue says tax sales can be held on the first Monday in April or the last Monday in August, depending on the county. We did not find Forrest County's sale date or interest rate on a page we could open, so we are leaving both out.

  • A landowner can redeem within two years after the sale under Miss. Code Ann. 27-45-3, as described in Mississippi Supreme Court opinions.
  • Land that finds no buyer goes to the State, and the Secretary of State handles it.
  • Business personal property has a separate rendition due April 1, with a mandatory 10% penalty for missing it.

sections.h2: What should a Forrest County seller expect?
sections.html:
Sellers in Hattiesburg and Petal often deal with timing around closing, a roll that has not caught up with a recent deed, and repairs that a conventional buyer's lender may flag. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so those repairs do not delay closing, though liens and unpaid taxes still must be cleared through title.

Before you list or accept any offer, gather the deed, the latest tax statement and any homestead paperwork, and call the Tax Collector at (601) 582-8228 to confirm what is owed. This is general information, not legal or tax advice.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Forrest County, MS?
faqs.a: Taxes are due on or before February 1 for property assessed the prior year. If February 1 is a weekend or legal holiday, payment is accepted the next Monday without penalty or interest.

faqs.q: Where is the Forrest County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: The Tax Collector is at 601 N. Main Street in downtown Hattiesburg, phone (601) 582-8228. The Tax Assessor is at the same address, phone (601) 545-6130.

faqs.q: When can I file homestead exemption in Forrest County?
faqs.a: Applications are accepted from January 2 to April 1. The county says it is a one-time filing unless something changes, and it does not apply to rental property.

faqs.q: How long does a new deed take to show on the Forrest County roll?
faqs.a: The county says it usually takes up to a year to see your property in your name after you buy, because mapping staff work the previous year's recorded deeds for the current land roll.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Forrest County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and a title company will confirm the amount. If the parcel was sold at a tax sale, Mississippi gives the owner two years from the sale to redeem.
